subject: Draft: Performance cycle communications, escalations, and exec approval path
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: people-ops@acme-example.com, projects@meritbench.co
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Draft: Performance cycle communications, escalations, and exec approval path

Team —

I put together a first-pass plan for the 2026 performance cycle communications and escalation path. The goal here is to provide a minimal set of synchronous approval points for pay/accelerators while keeping managers responsible for calibration. Key goals:

- Clear calendar (announcements, manager training, review window, calibration, finalization)
- Simple manager review form (one page) and rubric to reduce back-and-forth
- Explicit escalation matrix when manager/employee disagreements hit compensation thresholds
- Exec approval gates: Director sign-off for all >10% comp changes; VP + People sign-off for >20% or role changes

Attached: 2026-11-15_perf-cycle_comm_draft.docx, manager-review-form-v2.xlsx, exec-escalation-matrix.pdf

Asks:
1) Laura — can you weigh in on comm tone and timing (internal vs. all-hands)?
2) Stephanie — confirm the escalation thresholds are ok from a People & compliance perspective.
3) Marcus — do we need an engineering-specific rubric or can managers use the same manager-review-form-v2?
4) Dev — any product org constraints (feature freeze / availability) during the review window we should avoid?

Proposed high-level timeline (rough):
- 11/23: All-manager kickoff + training session (60m)
- 11/29: Company announcement (email + intranet)
- 12/01–12/13: Manager review window (two weeks)
- 12/16–12/20: Calibration & exec approvals
- 01/05: Final letters distributed

I’m available Tue/Wed for a short sync if needed. If we can get alignment this week I’ll post the comm and schedule manager training.

Thanks —
Jonas
VP, Product Strategy
Redwood Inference

Attachments: 2026-11-15_perf-cycle_comm_draft.docx, manager-review-form-v2.xlsx, exec-escalation-matrix.pdf

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 08:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft: Performance cycle communications, escalations, and exec approval path

On Sun, Nov 15, 2026 at 9:12 AM Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com> wrote:
> I put together a first-pass plan for the 2026 performance cycle communications and escalation path.

Thanks for pulling this together, Jonas — nicely scoped. Quick initial thoughts:

- Tone: Keep the public announcement focused on development and calibration rather than comp. We should preview timing and point managers to the FAQ for comp-related questions.
- Timing: 11/29 announcement is fine, but avoid the week of 11/30 for the manager training (we have product roadmap reviews then). Can we move the manager training to 11/24 or 12/02?
- Manager form: I like the condensed manager-review-form-v2.xlsx but request an optional "notes for calibration" field so managers can surface context.

I’ve added inline comments to the draft doc and added a short comms blurb you can drop into the email. I'll upload the marked file to the Drive folder.

Laura Bennett
Head of Internal Comms
Redwood Inference

Attachment note: uploaded a marked version to Drive (links below).

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: MeritBench Consulting <projects@meritbench.co>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft: Performance cycle communications, escalations, and exec approval path

Thanks — this is a good starting point. A few compliance/People items to call out:

1) Escalation thresholds: the >10% and >20% gates are okay, but People should be looped earlier for any promotion recommendations at Director level or above (we need a short promo packet).
2) Documentation: Managers must attach evidence for any comp >10% (last 12 months' goal attainment, recent 1:1 notes). We should add a checklist to manager-review-form-v2.xlsx.
3) Confidentiality: Communication should include a short blurb reminding managers about confidentiality and information access controls.
4) Timeline tweak: Calibration should be at least 48 hours after manager submissions to allow People to review escalations. So shift finalization window to 12/17–12/22; distribution 01/06 to avoid holidays.

I updated the exec-escalation-matrix.pdf with People contact points and added the checklist to the review form. See attachments.

Stephanie Nguyen
Head of People Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: exec-escalation-matrix.pdf (updated), manager-review-form-v2.xlsx (updated)

From: MeritBench Consulting <projects@meritbench.co>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft: Performance cycle communications, escalations, and exec approval path

Hi team —

Thanks for the invite to review. A few suggestions from our side after scanning the materials:

- Calibration rubric: add a short distribution chart (below-expectations / meets / exceeds / exceptional) with examples tailored to IC vs. Manager tracks. That reduces debate during calibration.
- Audit trail: include a single-page sign-off record per employee (who approved what and when) to simplify later audits.
- Manager training: recommend a 75-minute session with examples and 20 minutes Q&A; include a short pre-read for managers (3 slides).

We can run a 60m dry-run for the manager training on 11/24 if that works — we’ll need the final manager form a minimum of 48 hours before the dry-run.

Best,
Marta Alvarez
Senior Consultant, MeritBench Consulting
projects@meritbench.co

Attachment: MeritBench_calibration_examples.pdf

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: MeritBench Consulting <projects@meritbench.co>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft: Performance cycle communications, escalations, and exec approval path

Thanks all — good input and thanks to MeritBench for the calibration guidance. Quick summary and decisions (to capture agreement):

- Timeline: manager training dry-run 11/24 (60m, external-runner), company announcement 11/29, manager review 12/01–12/13, calibration & exec approval 12/17–12/22, distribution 01/06.
- Manager form: use manager-review-form-v2.xlsx (final attached) with added "notes for calibration" and People checklist.
- Escalation matrix: follow thresholds in exec-escalation-matrix.pdf; People to be looped for promotions Director+.
- Training: MeritBench will run dry-run on 11/24; full manager session to be scheduled after small edits.

Action items:
- Laura: finalize announcement text by 11/19 (I can take a pass if helpful).
- Stephanie: confirm promotion packet template and upload to Drive by 11/19.
- Marcus: confirm that the engineering rubric is acceptable by 11/20 or propose a specific modification.
- Dev: flag any blackout windows for the product org by 11/20.

If there are no objections I’ll mark this plan as approved and post the manager comm later this week.

—Jonas
VP, Product Strategy
Redwood Inference
